user.title: Microsoft Family Safety
user.description: Configure the integration. After Submit, Home Assistant opens Microsoft sign-in through a temporary authentication proxy and captures the OAuth redirect automatically. If Home Assistant is not reachable over HTTPS, local HTTP can be explicitly enabled for testing; Microsoft credentials are then not transport-encrypted on the local network.

data.allow_insecure_http_auth: Allow insecure local HTTP authentication (testing only)

auth.title: Manual Microsoft Family Safety authentication
auth.description:
Home Assistant could not use the secure browser-assisted login because no HTTPS Home Assistant URL is configured. Open this Microsoft URL, sign in, and paste the complete resulting redirect URL here:

{auth_url}

reauth_confirm.title: Reauthenticate Microsoft Family Safety
reauth_confirm.description: The stored Microsoft sign-in is incomplete, expired, or revoked. Continue to run the complete sign-in again and renew both the mobile refresh token and the Family web session.

reauth_full_confirm.title: Reauthenticate Microsoft Family Safety
reauth_full_confirm.description: The stored Microsoft authentication is incomplete, expired, or revoked. Continue to renew both the mobile OAuth refresh token and the Family web session. If this Home Assistant instance is only reachable over a private local HTTP URL, enable the local HTTP test option below.

data.allow_insecure_http_auth: Allow insecure local HTTP authentication (testing only)

reauth_success.title: Microsoft Family Safety sign-in completed
reauth_success.description: Microsoft authentication completed successfully and the new credentials are ready to be saved. Select Submit to finish the reauthentication.

check_mobile_proxy.title: Microsoft sign-in
check_mobile_proxy.description: Sign in with the Microsoft account that manages the family. Keep the opened authentication window open. After the visible sign-in completes, Home Assistant will automatically switch to a waiting screen while Microsoft Family SSO finishes.

auth_success.title: Microsoft Family Safety sign-in completed
auth_success.description: Both Microsoft authentication phases completed successfully. Select Continue to create the integration.

error.no_redirect_url: Please enter a valid redirect URL.
error.native_https_required: Automatic browser authentication normally requires HTTPS. For local testing you can explicitly enable insecure local HTTP authentication.
error.native_http_not_local: Insecure HTTP authentication is allowed only through localhost, .local, or a private/local IP address.

abort.native_auth_failed: The Microsoft web authentication did not complete successfully.
abort.native_auth_state_lost: The browser authentication flow expired. Please start again.
abort.native_auth_unavailable: Native web authentication could not be loaded: {error}
abort.native_oauth_failed: The Microsoft Family Safety OAuth login did not complete successfully.
abort.wrong_account: A different Microsoft account was used. Please reauthenticate the same Family Safety account.

check_mobile_proxy.description: Sign in with the Microsoft account that manages the family. After mobile OAuth succeeds, the same browser tab is redirected automatically into the Family web-session phase. After the visible Microsoft sign-in has finished, Home Assistant may need up to about 60 seconds to complete Microsoft's silent Family SSO and capture the Family session. Keep the browser window open and do not press Open website again while this is in progress.

check_proxy.description: Home Assistant is establishing the authenticated account.microsoft.com Family session. If Microsoft silent SSO needs to recover, the proxy retries the top-level account navigation automatically.

progress.family_sso: Microsoft sign-in is complete. Home Assistant is waiting for Microsoft Family SSO to finish in the open authentication window. This can take up to about 60 seconds. Keep the Microsoft window open; no action is required.
